2. Bring the work into one place without rebuilding your setup
3. Choose a session that fits the day you actually have
4. Add friction before the automatic scroll
5. Reset the plan when the day changes
A deadline is not a plan: how to make time for your tasks
A deadline is not a plan: how to make time for your tasks | Nonlate
A first session is not a promise that the entire task will be finished. Leave time before the actual deadline for the work you discover along the way.

A plan can still lose to a familiar habit: open your phone, tap a social app, and forget why you picked it up. Nonlate’s deadline-aware blocking can interrupt selected distracting apps when an eligible unfinished task is overdue or inside your chosen due-work window.

Add a manual task, or connect a supported source in Nonlate’s integration settings. School tasks might come from Canvas or Moodle; work might already live in Notion, Todoist or Google Tasks. You can keep using the original service while bringing supported task information into Nonlate.

At the end of a session, ask what is actually finished and what remains. Keep unfinished work visible. When a connected task changes, check its current state and allow for the provider’s sync behavior.

Before starting, decide on one concrete next action, such as opening the assignment brief and outlining the first argument. That is a way to approach the session, not a separate name you have to give the plan.
Bring the work into one place
Calendar connections help you see commitments in Schedule. Calendar events do not trigger blocking, and a busy calendar is not the same as an unfinished task.
Check the imported deadline before planning around it. Available fields and sync timing depend on the provider, permissions, plan and device. A change in another app may not appear immediately.
Choose a real deadline, plan one manageable session before it, and select one distracting app you want to interrupt when due work needs attention.
Choose when to work on that task and a duration you can realistically protect. Menu wording can vary by app version. The resulting plan is based on the task’s name.
Connections, sync behavior and blocking controls vary by platform and plan. See current plans or contact support for setup help.
For permission setup, platform differences and troubleshooting, read how to block distracting apps until your tasks are done. Keep essential communication and emergency tools accessible.
If Tuesday afternoon gets taken over by something urgent, revisit the session. Choose another realistic time instead of changing Friday’s real deadline just to make the list look less urgent.

Imagine an essay due Friday at 5 p.m. Leave Friday at 5 p.m. as the deadline. Then plan time for that essay on Tuesday afternoon, when you have room to begin. The session appears under the essay task’s name.

Keep the real deadline, then choose a separate time to work on the task. Start with a small session you can actually keep. In Nonlate, use Tasks for the work and its deadline, Planner to plan a session, and Schedule to see how that session fits around your day.
Look at Schedule for classes, meetings and other commitments. Leave room for travel, meals and the ordinary gaps between activities.

Planning a session is not, by itself, a command to block every distraction during that session. The task’s deadline and your blocking settings determine whether due-work blocking applies. If you need a fixed time-of-day restriction, do not assume a planned session creates one.
Real deadlines, at the moment they matter. Built for school, work, and everyday life.
Separate the deadline from the work session
Start with one important unfinished task, rather than trying to schedule your whole list at once.
The goal is not a perfectly packed calendar. It is knowing which task you will return to next, when you have time for it, and which distractions you want to put aside.
The same distinction works for a report, a job application or a household task. “When must this be done?” and “When will I work on it?” are different questions.
This guide is published by the maker of Nonlate. It explains a practical workflow, not a guarantee that an app will finish your work for you.
This translation is machine-assisted. For unclear wording, read the English version or contact Nonlate support.
Try it with one task this week
Turn a deadline into a realistic work session. Use Nonlate to bring tasks together, plan when to start and interrupt distractions when unfinished work is due.
Use blocking as a reminder to follow through

You can return to the task or use an available timed break. Marking a task complete removes it as a blocking reason; another qualifying unfinished task can still keep blocking active. Nonlate does not verify that an assignment was submitted or that the underlying work was actually done.
Your plan uses the task’s name. You do not need to invent a separate plan title, and scheduling a session does not change the task’s deadline.
how to block distracting apps until your tasks are done
“Due Friday” tells you when the work must be finished. It does not tell you what to do on Tuesday afternoon. That gap is where a task can sit untouched while the week fills up.
